egypt_status.evidence_source: EPPO lists Puccinia sorghi as present in Egypt; the available distribution record does not provide a current Egyptian governorate-level survey or severity estimate.
egypt_status.evidence_date_note: EPPO's distribution entry is based on available historical and disease-map records; current local prevalence should be verified through Egyptian field surveillance.

host_and_life_cycle.infection_source: Wind-dispersed urediniospores can repeatedly infect maize; the pathogen has a two-host life cycle involving maize and Oxalis.

early_stage: Minute pale-yellow or chlorotic flecks on leaves
Small tan spots that become slightly raised
characteristic_sign: Circular to oval or slightly elongated powdery pustules
Pustules rupture the leaf epidermis and release powdery spores
Pustules may occur on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
late_stage: Pustules darken to brown-black as teliospores replace urediniospores
Numerous pustules give the leaf a rusty or peppered appearance
Severe infections cause yellowing, premature drying, and death of leaves or leaf sheaths
other_visible_locations: Husks, tassels, and stalks may show pustules, although leaves are the main diagnostic surface
Pustules can form in bands when infection occurs while leaves are emerging from the whorl
image_annotation_targets: number of pustules per leaf area
pustule colour: orange-brown versus dark brown-black
circular, oval, or elongated pustule shape
pustule bands associated with whorl infection
chlorosis and percentage of prematurely dead leaf tissue

symptoms: dark brown to black telial pustules

pustule_size.note: Size and shape can vary between common rust and southern rust and between plant tissues.

distribution_on_plant: Most conspicuous on leaves and often visible on both leaf surfaces. Severe infections may extend to leaf sheaths, husks, tassels, and stalks.
progression: Minute chlorotic flecks appear on susceptible leaf tissue.
Flecks enlarge into tan, raised spots.
Cinnamon-brown powdery uredinial pustules break through the epidermis and release spores.
Pustules multiply and may occur in scattered patches or bands.
As the plant matures, pustules turn dark brown or black as teliospores develop.
Severe disease causes chlorosis, premature leaf drying, reduced photosynthetic area, and early leaf or sheath death.

environment.humidity: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness favour rust development; humidity above 95% is reported as highly favourable in disease-management guidance.
environment.temperature: Mild temperatures around 16–25 °C favour Puccinia sorghi; the optimum range is commonly reported near 16–23 °C.
environment.leaf_wetness: Dew, rain, and persistent surface moisture support infection and sporulation.
environment.egypt_context: These mild, humid conditions may occur during suitable Egyptian maize growing periods, but the reviewed Egypt record did not provide an Egypt-specific weather threshold or seasonal prevalence study.
environment.crop_stage: Monitoring is especially important from approximately the six-leaf stage through tasseling.

egypt_specific_distribution.governorates: No reliable governorate-level distribution was identified in the reviewed sources.
egypt_specific_distribution.field_surveillance_note: Do not infer national incidence or severity from the presence-only record. Local confirmation requires field sampling and pathogen identification.

similar_diseases.name: Southern Rust of Maize
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Often has smaller, more orange to reddish pustules concentrated mainly on the upper leaf surface; microscopic or molecular confirmation may be needed.

similar_diseases.name: Maydis Leaf Blight / Southern Leaf Blight
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Produces flat tan or brown diamond-shaped and rectangular necrotic lesions, not discrete powdery pustules.

similar_diseases.name: Northern Leaf Blight
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Produces long grey-green to tan cigar-shaped lesions rather than numerous raised rust pustules.

diagnostic_caution: Pustule colour and distribution can overlap with southern rust caused by Puccinia polysora. Confirm species by microscopy of urediniospores and teliospores or by molecular testing when an Egypt-specific diagnosis is required.
